pages.ja:
「桜、入るぞ」
返事を待たずにドアを開ける。
そもそもこのドアを開ける時、妹の返事を待った事など一度もない。

pages.en:
“Sakura. I'm coming in.”

He opens the door without waiting for an answer.

For that matter, he has never once waited for his sister to answer before opening this door.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m coming in, Sakura.”

pages.ja:
「なんだ、まだ帰ってきてないのか。本当に困ったもんだな、あいつ」
舌打ちをしながら室内に踏み入る。
間桐慎二は壁に爪を立てながら、視力を失った犬のように、ぐるぐると妹の部屋を徘徊する。

pages.en:
“What, she still isn't back? Honestly, what am I supposed to do with her?”

Clicking his tongue, he steps inside.

Shinji Matou circles endlessly through his sister's room, clawing at the walls like a dog that has lost its sight.

“What, she’s not home yet?
What a slug.”
She really is a problem.”
He clucks his tongue and walks into the room.
Scratching at the wall, Matou Shinji wanders through his sister’s room like a blind dog.

pages.ja:
「桜。今日も地下か。ああ、僕をさしおいてまた下で何かやっているんだろ」
返答のない質問を繰り返す。
部屋には誰もいない。
ここ数日、彼の妹は屋敷に帰ってきていない。
主不在の部屋が無人である事は判りきっているというのに、間桐慎二は室内を徘徊する。

pages.en:
“Sakura. Are you down in the basement again today? Of course. You're down there doing something without me again, aren't you?”

He repeats a question that will receive no answer.

The room is empty.

His sister has not returned to the mansion for several days.

Shinji Matou knows perfectly well that the room must be deserted in its owner's absence, yet still he prowls through it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Sakura. Are you in the basement again? What’re you doing down there, ignoring me?”
He keeps asking questions that will not be answered.
There is no one in the room.
His sister has not been home the past few days.
It is obvious that the master of this room is not here, but Shinji wanders through it all the same.

pages.ja:
「いつも通り。ハハ、まったく、ホントにいつも通りじゃないか！」
ふと手に触れた時計を投げつけた。
ガラスの砕ける音は、思った以上に耳障りだった。
pages.jaRuby:
「いつも通り。ハハ、まったく、ホントにいつも通りじゃないか！」
ふと手に触れた時計を投げつけた。

pages.en:
“The same as ever. Hah—hahaha! It really is exactly the same as ever!”

His hand brushes against a clock, and he hurls it away.

The shattering glass grates upon his ears more harshly than he expected.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s just like always. Haha, it really is like always!”
He throws the clock that touches his hand.
The sound of shattering glass is more annoying than he thought.

pages.ja:
「何処いってんだよ。兄貴に内緒でさ……」
怒りを吐き出すように物を放る。
……それもいつもの事だ。
これはここ数年、日課になっていた代償行為にすぎない。
彼が真実を知った三年前に始まった、自分と、妹を赦す為の、精一杯の抵抗だった。

pages.en:
“Where have you gone without telling your brother…?”

He throws one object after another, as though casting out his anger with them.

…That too is nothing unusual.

For the past several years, this compensatory ritual has been part of his daily life.

It is the only resistance he could muster—an attempt to forgive himself and his sister—begun three years ago, when he learned the truth.

pages.ja: 彼が生まれた時、間桐の血は既に役目を終えていた。
pages.jaRuby: 彼が生まれた時、間桐の血は既に役目を終えていた。
pages.en: —By the time he was born, the blood of Matou had already fulfilled its purpose.
pages.mirrorMoon: The Matou bloodline came to an end when he was born.

pages.ja:
貴い血族である彼らは力を失い、間桐はただの“人間”になり下がった。
特別なものは蓄えられた知識だけ。
かつての魔道の名門は、この極東の地で人知れず滅びる定めとなったのだ。

pages.en:
The once-noble bloodline had lost its power, and the Matous had fallen into being mere “human beings.”

Accumulated knowledge was the only special thing left to them.

The once-prestigious house of magecraft was fated to perish unnoticed here in the Far East.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The noble family lost its power, becoming mere humans.
The only special thing is the accumulated knowledge.
The once noble family of magi is fated to perish in this Far East country.

pages.ja:
その事実を、幼いながらも彼は聞かされていた。
間桐は秘跡を伝える一族であり、特別な存在だったと。
既に過去形。
間桐には魔術を扱える者はおらず、今後はまっとうな人として社会に関わっていくのだと。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
He had been told as much while still a child.

The Matous were a special family, one that transmitted the Mysteries.

But that belonged to the past.

No one among them remained capable of magecraft, and in the future they would enter society as ordinary, respectable people.
pages.mirrorMoon:

The Matou family was a family that passed down secret techniques.
But it is all in past tense now.
As the Matou are no longer able to use magic, they are to blend into society as ordinary people.

pages.ja:
だが、彼はそう思わなかった。
確かに魔術回路とやらは途絶え、魔術という秘跡を実践する事もない。
魔術師としての間桐は父の代で終わり、自分には間桐の名を継ぐ資格はないとも判っている。
しかし、それでも間桐には秘跡の記録がある。
途絶えたのは血筋だけ、蓄えた知識は失われてはいないのだ。

pages.en:
But the boy did not see it that way.

Their so-called Magic Circuits might have died out, and they might never again practice the mysteries of magecraft.

He understood that the Matou line of mages would end with his father, and that he himself lacked the qualifications to carry on the Matou name.

Even so, the Matous still possessed records of the Mysteries.

Only the bloodline had failed. The knowledge they had amassed was not lost.
pages.mirrorMoon:

But the Matou family still has the records.

pages.ja:
それは、少年にとって十分“特別”な事だった。
自分は他の人間とは違う。
間桐家は選ばれた一族だ。
たとえ魔力を失い魔術師でなくなったとしても、その価値に変わりはない。
自分はその特別な家の子供として、特別に生きていくのだと誇りを持った。
魔術師として落第点だろうが、選ばれた家の子供である事は確かなのだから、と。

pages.en:
—To the boy, that was sufficiently “special.”

He was different from other people.

The Matou family was a chosen bloodline.

Even if they had lost their magical energy and ceased to be mages, their worth remained unchanged.

He took pride in being the child of that special house, and believed that he too would lead a special life.

He might be a failure as a mage, but he was indisputably the child of a chosen family.
pages.mirrorMoon:

pages.ja:
……その選ばれた家に、いつしか新しい子供が紛れ込んでいた。
父は身寄りのない少女を引き取り、養女にしたという。
もう十年以上前の話だ。
桜という名の少女は、その日から彼の妹になった。

…Then, before he knew it, another child had slipped into that chosen house.

His father had taken in an orphaned girl and adopted her.

That was more than ten years ago.

From that day onward, the girl named Sakura became his sister.
pages.mirrorMoon:

pages.ja:
初め、彼は妹を毛嫌いしていた。
特別である間桐の家に異分子を入れたくなかったからだ。
だが日が経つにつれ、彼は妹を容認しはじめる。
桜という少女は無口で、凡庸で、番犬程度のことしかできない。
そんな存在を敵視する事など時間の無駄だし、ある程度愚鈍な方が愛らしい。

pages.en:
At first, he detested her.

He did not want a foreign element introduced into the special house of Matou.

As the days passed, however, he began to tolerate his sister.

The girl named Sakura was silent, ordinary, and capable of little more than serving as a watchdog.

Treating such a creature as an enemy would be a waste of time. Besides, a certain measure of stupidity made her endearing.

彼は書物をあさり、身につかない魔道を覚え、間桐の後継者を自認していった。

pages.en:
He devoured books, memorized magecraft he could never master, and came to regard himself as the Matou heir.

He alone was permitted inside the Matou study.

His sister was adopted and could never have been chosen as successor. She possessed no right to read its books.

Without ever learning the sole body of knowledge the Matous still possessed, she would live and die as an ordinary person.

That too provided immense satisfaction to his pride.

pages.ja:
魔術師の家系において、後継者はただ一人。
それを知っていた彼は、自分の妹が自分と切り離されて育てられている事に疑問をもたなかった。
魔術を習うのは一人だけ。
なら、妹が自分から離されているのは当然の事だったから。

pages.en:
In a lineage of mages, there could be only one successor.

Because he knew this, he never questioned why his sister was raised apart from him.

Only one child would learn magecraft.

It was therefore natural that his sister should be separated from him.

Yes.

Put plainly, he pitied her.

They lived in the same house and shared the same parents, yet he rejoiced that he alone was “special” and felt sorry for the sister who had not been chosen.

It was the condescending pity of a superior—and for him, the firmest foundation of his pride as an older brother.

In time, the brother came to pity his sister and treat her with affection.

That sister always lowered her head, averting her eyes from him.

Believing her behavior was born of shyness, he loved his helpless little sister.

Until the day he learned this thing called the truth.

pages.en:
A room whose existence had been hidden from him.

Knowledge he had never been taught.

Talent he had never been granted.

All of it was there.

A girl stood in the center of the room.

Something black writhed around her, and their terrifying grandfather stood nearby.

His father glanced at the intruder with an expression the boy had never seen before—the look one gives a nuisance.

pages.en:
His life changed completely.

His father, deciding there was no longer any need for concealment, focused openly on Sakura alone, more than ever.

His sister said nothing and merely lowered her head, just as she always had.

Still behaving exactly as before, as though trying to escape his gaze, she spoke.

“…I'm sorry, Shinji.”

He laughed.

It was funny from the bottom of his heart.

Funny enough to make him want to destroy everything.

The creature he had regarded as a pet was the true master, and he himself had been nothing but a clown.

Which of them was absurd, him or her?

Surely both.

He returned to the mansion upon ground where everything had been overturned—and there, he was forced to understand.
